title: Tiered Variant Routing Operational Guidance
summary: Operational guidance for implementing and operating tiered routing with model-variant fallbacks and cross-region spillover. Focuses on control-plane responsibilities, runtime primitives, telemetry-driven policies, and an actionable on-call runbook.
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures the operational playbook and architecture notes for a tiered variant routing system: how we route requests across model variants and capacity tiers, how the control plane coordinates degradations, and how to safely spill traffic regionally when local capacity is depleted. Target audience: platform engineers, SREs, and solutions engineers responsible for runtime routing and incident response.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Maintain highest possible availability for customer traffic with bounded latency regression.
  - Provide clear operator actions for stepwise degradation (soft -> hard) and recovery.
  - Keep unit-cost visibility and avoid unbounded cost when spilling across regions.
- Non-goals:
  - Complete ML-quality evaluation of every variant (handled by applied-ml).
  - Replacing customer-side throttles or client backpressure (clients should still be resilient).

Assumptions:
- Each route has an ordered list of model variants (e.g., v2-highperf, v2-quantized, v1-legacy) with compatibility metadata (latency, tokens/sec, model-size, quantizable).
- Capacity tiers exist per-region: reserved (dedicated), burst (shared preemptible), and overflow (cross-region spill).
- Control plane exposes APIs for: setRoutingWeights(route, variantWeights), setTierLimit(region, tier, qps), and emergencyCutover(region, targetVariant).
- Telemetry available: p50/p95 latency, tail latency, queue-depth, token-rate, error-rate (502/503/timeout), model-cpu/gpu utilization, per-variant inference failures, and cost-per-token estimate.

Logical state machine for route degradation:
- Normal (green): prefer best-quality variant on reserved capacity. Autoscale keeps latency SLO.
- Congestion (amber): if queue-depth > threshold OR p95 > SLO*1.2 for 30s -> trigger soft degradation: shift X% to degraded-compatible variants + enable batching suggestions.
- Strained (red): if amber persists 5m OR error-rate increases -> escalate to hard degradation: increase weight to cheaper variants, enable cross-region spill to nearest low-latency region (bounded by cost budget), reduce max tokens per request for burst tier.
- Emergency (black): catastrophic failure (region outage) -> immediate cutover to fallback global model family and disable non-essential routes.

Degradation primitives (control-plane operations):
- Weight shifts: atomic update to variant weight vector with gradual ramp (e.g., 10% steps / 30s) to avoid thundering.
- Tier gating: limit traffic into tier by qps or concurrency. Tier stepdown sequence: reserved -> burst -> overflow.
- Request shaping: enforce per-request token cap, priority tags, and sampling rate for heavy ops (rerank/long-completion).
- Model slimming: switch to quantized variant or smaller context window when latency/throughput critical.
- Regional spill: route X% of traffic to target region with affinity bucketing to maintain session stickiness where possible.

Prioritization matrix for variants and routes:
- Each route has metadata: criticality (p0..p3), cost-sensitivity (high/medium/low), latency-tolerance (ms), model-dependence (strict/soft).
- Policy example: p0 routes (auth, payment, safety) -> never spill cross-region unless emergency; prefer lower-latency fallback in-region. p2/p3 routes -> allow regional spill and quantized variants earlier.

Operational checks and preconditions before enabling spillover:
- Verify target region healthy: control-plane heartbeat ok, model binaries loaded, GPU utilization < 60%, no ongoing deployments.
- Verify cost budget for overflow is not exceeded (daily/weekly burn threshold).
- Notify dependent teams (via #platform-incidents and short alert) with planned spill window.

Observability and SLOs to drive decisions (telemetry thresholds):
- Primary signals:
  - Route p95 latency > SLO*1.2 for >30s -> soft degrade.
  - Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% for >1m -> investigate model/infra; consider hard degrade.
  - Queue depth > 80% capacity for >2m -> throttle/burst gating.
- Secondary signals:
  - Token cost per minute trending up 40% vs baseline -> consider stepping down to cheaper variants.
  - Cross-region network RTT > 100ms additional -> avoid spill to that region unless emergency.

Runbook: step-by-step for on-call (fast path):
1) Detect: automated alert for route.p95 or queue depth. Open incident in JIRA (use template linked_artifacts).
2) Initial triage (5 minutes): check per-variant failure counts, recent deploys, infra alarms. Slack #platform-oncall with short blurb.
3) Soft degrade (if thresholds hit): execute setRoutingWeights(route, weights) to shift 20% -> degraded variant. Document change in incident ticket.
4) Monitor (10 minutes): if metrics improve, keep gradual ramp (next 20%). If not, prepare hard degrade.
5) Hard degrade: gate burst tier, increase quantized variant to 60-80% depending on route criticality, enable cross-region spill to preferred region at 10% increments.
6) Cost safety net: if overflow cost estimate > budget, automatically rollback spill by 50% and notify finance-owner channel.
7) Recovery: once p95 < SLO and stable for 10m, ramp weights back to primary variant in reversed steps.
8) Postmortem: attach timeline of weight/tier changes, deltas in token-cost, latencies, and any manual overrides.

Automations and safe-guards to implement (items for infra backlog):
- Automated progressive ramp with rollback on increased error-rate during ramp.
- Dry-run mode: simulate weight updates without traffic redirection (use traffic shadowing).
- Rate-limited control-plane API keys and audit logs for all weight/tier changes.
- Canary for cross-region spill functionality: periodically divert 0.1% traffic to exercise path.
- Quick rollback knob: a single boolean toggle per-route to return to primary-only routing.

Failure scenarios and playbook highlights:
- Scenario A: sustained high latency due to model hot-path (no infra failure)
  - Action: ramp quantized variant + impose temporary token cap. Notify model owners.
- Scenario B: reserved capacity exhausted across region (GPU constraint)
  - Action: open burst tier; if burst can't absorb, enable 20% spill to region-B and monitor cost.
- Scenario C: full region outage (network partition)
  - Action: emergency cutover to global-fallback family, disable region affinity, escalate to SEV process.

Clients and compatibility notes:
- Clients must tolerate eventual consistency in routing decisions (weights can change). Use retry with backoff for transient 5xx.
- Sessions: prefer sticky hashing by session-id for short-lived stickiness; document fallback when session affinity cannot be maintained.

Testing and exercises:
- Quarterly chaos drills: simulate reserved capacity loss and exercise spill sequence.
- Pre-launch validation: run shadowing to measure quality delta between model variants for the route.
- KPI dashboards: per-route cost, p95, error-rate, cross-region spill volume.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What is the canonical cost budget window for overflow (daily vs weekly)? (Owner: Finance/Product)
- How aggressively should we quantize for p0 routes before affecting model correctness? (Owner: Applied-ML)
- Should we offer per-customer spill/deny toggles in the console or keep it platform-only? (Owner: Product-Dedicated)

Next steps / TODOs:
- Implement automated ramp+rollback feature in control-plane (JIRA-INF-842).
- Add billing alert hook to overflow policy.
- Schedule the next chaos drill and invite applied-ml and customer-success.

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- Consider using affinity buckets tied to geo+model-hash to minimize cold KV-cache misses post-spill.
- Short-term hack: allow targeted transient permissive-routing for long-running customer jobs to avoid mid-run interruptions.
- Keep runbook steps concise for on-call — long explanations go into Confluence.

References:
- Internal: routing-configs repo PR #98, Confluence page CONFLUENCE-12345 for policy definitions.
- Slack threads: #platform-routing thread on 2024-11-02.

Contact for follow-up: Maya Chen (owner), Diego Alvarez (SRE lead), Priya Nair (product).
